newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: No polls if Cambodia's king steps down - co-premier.
newsitem.headline: No polls if Cambodia's king steps down - co-premier.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen said on Friday that local and general elections would have to be cancelled if King Norodom Sihanouk decided to abdicate, a move that would allow him to re-enter the world of politics.

"If the king abdicates we should cancel all elections, both local and national elections in 1997 and 1998, because we must gather together to solve the throne crisis first," Hun Sen told a meeting of fisheries officials.
Parliament would have to decide whether the country should continue as a monarchy or become a republic, he said.

Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) shares power with the royalist FUNCINPEC party of Sihanouk's son, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in an uneasy coalition government formed after a U.N.-run poll in 1993 ended decades of war and civil strife.
Some analysts believe Hun Sen and the formerly communist CPP fear the king might step down to lead royalists to victory at the next elections.
"If His Majesty wants to abdicate and become a politician, he must resign from the royalists," Hun Sen said.

Sihanouk, who is in China for a periodic medical checkup and treatment, said last month he had been thinking of abdicating following mounting attacks on the royal family, himself and his achievements.
But the 74-year-old monarch, who rules but does not govern, pledged he would never take part in the general elections or form a party for the polls.
